title: AI Strategy, Risk Appetite and Value
summary: How boards decide where AI should and should not be used, test management's business cases, and set a risk appetite that balances innovation against conduct, prudential and operational risk.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How boards decide where AI should and should not be used, test management's business cases, and set a risk appetite that balances innovation against conduct, prudential and operational risk.
Learning Objectives: Challenge management's AI strategy and claimed benefits
Set an AI risk appetite with measurable limits and escalation triggers
Weigh innovation against conduct, prudential and operational risk
Syllabus: Questions to ask of an AI strategy: purpose, benefit, cost, dependency and exit
Drafting a risk appetite statement: in-scope uses, prohibited uses and limits
Avoiding hype and paralysis: pilots and staged adoption
Investment, capability and talent decisions for board approval
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors and board committee members, especially on risk, audit and technology committees
Executive directors and senior managers accountable for AI, risk and compliance
Company secretaries and heads of governance supporting board oversight
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No technical background in AI or data science is required.
Core Reading: OECD, Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (2019, revised 2024)
NIST, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) (2023)
FSB, The Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence (2024)
